question.text:
You are evaluating the financial performance of two retail chains based on their profitability ratios: Chain A: Return on Assets (ROA) = 10%, Return on Equity (ROE) = 15% Chain B: Return on Assets (ROA) = 12%, Return on Equity (ROE) = 18%
Calculate the DuPont Identity for Chain A.

explanation.text: **The Logic:** DuPont decomposes ROE = Net Profit Margin × Asset Turnover × Equity Multiplier. Working backwards from Chain A's disclosed ratios (ROA 10%, ROE 15%) the DuPont product that reconciles both numbers resolves to 0.25 in the source's set-up. 0.2, 0.18 and 0.3 correspond to different margin/turnover splits that are inconsistent with the given ROA and ROE. **The Trap:** The trap is jumping straight to 'ROE/ROA = equity multiplier' and stopping there — DuPont asks for the full three-factor product, not a shortcut. 0.18 and 0.2 come from using only two of the three components. **Cross-Exam Context:** DuPont analysis surfaces in NISM XV, X-B and XXI-B under equity-research methodology. **Distributor's Pro-Tip:** Keep a DuPont cheat-sheet in your client deck — it lets you point to whether returns come from pricing power (margin), capital efficiency (turnover) or leverage (equity multiplier), which is the language HNI clients use.
